shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The row is bounded to the single chazon header verse: “The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.” (web:Isa.1.1). The Hebrew opens with חֲזוֹן֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier), a superscription noun naming the seer, his father, and the four-king regnal window, with no imperative, vocative, or divine-speech formula of its own; the next verse opens a fresh imperative summons (“Hear, heavens, and listen, earth”, web:Isa.1.2), which is the row's own seam.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the header into the following summons unit was rejected because the header verse carries no imperative or address of its own and names a distinct royal-regnal frame absent from verse 2.

shipped_row.device_notes: Both superscriptions carry the same relative clause, אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה, byte-identical at three verses book-wide — oshb:Isa.1.1, oshb:Isa.2.1, and oshb:Isa.13.1, the massa hinge (sweep: 3 verses, byte). The two superscriptions share the seer's name and the Judah/Jerusalem object; what distinguishes them is the header-noun class — חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1 / oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier) — together with the regnal window naming Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier), which has no counterpart in 2:1.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the double imperative-vocative summons שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, byte tier), “Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh has spoken” (web:Isa.1.2), calling cosmic witnesses to the case before any content of the charge is stated; verse 3's ox/donkey analogy completes the witness-testimony frame (“The ox knows his owner… but Israel doesn't know”, web:Isa.1.3). The row closes before the hoy-onset indictment proper begins at web:Isa.1.4.
